facts.text: BlockedUnlockPickupEnv is registered as MiniGrid-BlockedUnlockPickup-v0 with the entry point minigrid.envs:BlockedUnlockPickupEnv
The seven actions are left 0, right 1, forward 2, pickup 3, drop 4, toggle 5 and done 6
The action space is Discrete(len(actions)), i.e. Discrete(7)
The observation space is a Dict of image = Box(low=0, high=255, shape=(agent_view_size, agent_view_size, 3), dtype=uint8), direction = Discrete(4) and the mission space
The direction is 0 right, 1 down, 2 left, 3 up (DIR_TO_VEC), and the direction string map is '>', 'V', '<', '^'
Each tile is encoded as (OBJECT_IDX, COLOR_IDX, STATE) and the door STATE is 0 open, 1 closed, 2 locked
OBJECT_TO_IDX maps unseen 0, empty 1, wall 2, floor 3, door 4, key 5, ball 6, box 7, goal 8, lava 9, agent 10; COLOR_TO_IDX maps red 0, green 1, blue 2, purple 3, yellow 4, grey 5

step increments step_count and then branches on the action: left decrements the direction, right increments it, forward moves when the front cell is empty or can be overlapped, pickup and drop move an object, toggle activates the front cell, and the done action does nothing
The episode is truncated when step_count reaches max_steps
BlockedUnlockPickupEnv ends the episode when the agent picks up the target box, with the success reward
The room grid is (room_size - 1) * num_rows + 1 high and (room_size - 1) * num_cols + 1 wide
BlockedUnlockPickupEnv uses two rooms of size 6 (num_rows 1, num_cols 2, so a 6 x 11 grid) and max_steps = 16 * room_size**2 when it is not given
The generated grid puts a box in the right room, a locked door between the rooms, a ball that blocks the door, a key in the left room and the agent in the left room

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the mission colour and the initial world, and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws its colours with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's generator, so a seed gives different worlds on the two

gaps: the world is a 6 x 11 two-room grid with a locked door, a ball, a key and a target box; it is a simplified stand-in for the upstream generator and was never compared with a run of the upstream environment (the upstream needs numpy, gymnasium and pygame-ce, which the gate does not have)
simulated time does not advance: MiniGrid is turn-based, so timestep_ms is 0 and a tick is one action

the image is encoded with the constants of the clone (7 x 7 x 3, OBJECT_TO_IDX/COLOR_TO_IDX/STATE_TO_IDX), but the agent's view is fully visible: no view-slicing occlusion (process_vis) and no partial observability behind walls is modelled
the mission text is drawn from the six colour names of COLOR_NAMES; upstream samples it from a MissionSpace, so the text is the same kind of string but not the same distribution
the clone exposes no get_state/set_state (it has a state hash only, minigrid/minigrid_env.py:159), so snapshot and restore are not offered and determinism is 'seeded', not 'exact'
rendering is not modelled and no physical device is modelled; nothing was validated against a device

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
